[Discussion] What recent successful AAA games you think were risky in at least the eyes of publishers?

Call of Duty Black Ops 3.

Hear me out on this: the last 2 games in the series were both considered to be less popular and had less sales than the previous titles. To Activision, the series could look like it's going downhill fast.

Advanced warfare was to spring new life but ultimately failed to do so, even with the new mechanics. Black ops 3 had the same mechanics more or less dumbed down, and from a neutral standpoint all the features packed in there could have resulted in a Jack of all trades effect where the entire game was just average.

Activision needed a game that was fantastic in order to effectively maintain the franchise. The new 3 year developement cycle (another potentially risky plan) cost Activision more money to pay the devs for three years while they work, a much larger investment than paying a dev for one year and then releasing a game.

The last two years generally being regarded as flops, this third year in the cycle did spell out whether or not the other 2 games undoubtedly in development were worth the continued investment. Had this game failed, the call of duty of 2017 might have been cancelled, and the franchise set to only appear once every other year to preserve costs and protect from over saturation.

To a similar degree, the new assassins creed can also be considered (unity was a clunky mess for a while, how has that affected the company's future profits etc. Etc.)
